overview.description: Mus is a popular Spanish game of Basque origin, played by four players in partnerships. It is unusual among vying games in that it is played without money and with partnerships. The game involves drawing cards and betting on who has the best hand in four categories: Grande (high), Chica (low), Pares (pairs), and Juego (game). It features extensive bluffing and a complex system of signals.

history.origins: Mus originated in the Basque region of Spain. The name may derive from the Basque word 'musu' meaning 'kiss' or from the Spanish 'mus' meaning 'muzzle'. It became one of the most popular card games in Spain.
timeline: 20th Century: Became one of Spain's most popular card games
Present: Widely played in Spain and by Spanish communities worldwide
history.evolution: The game has developed an extensive system of signals (signos) that partners use to communicate their hands. Many variants exist with different signal systems.
history.cultural: A deeply cultural game in Spain, particularly in the Basque Country, Navarre, and La Rioja. Played in social clubs, bars, and family gatherings. The bluffing and signaling aspects make it a game of psychological skill.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
setup.deck: 40-card Spanish pack. Suits: Swords, Batons, Cups, Coins. Cards: Rey (King), Caballo (Horse/Queen), Sota (Jack), 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, Ace. Note: 3s are equivalent to Kings, 2s are equivalent to Aces.
setup.equipment: 40-card Spanish deck, small stones or counters (piedras) for scoring.
setup.dealing: 4 cards to each player, one at a time, anticlockwise. The player to dealer's right is the 'mano' (first to speak in betting).

rules.objective: Be the first team to reach 40 points (winning a game). Win two games to win the match.
rules.gameplay: Deal 4 cards each. Optional Mus phase: all four may agree to discard one to four cards and receive replacements. Four betting rounds follow in order (Grande, Chica, Pares, Juego); mano may pass or bet; opponents may fold, see, or raise. Órdago stakes the whole game on one category. Showdown: compare hands in each category; first team to 40 points wins the game.
keyRules: Four categories: Grande, Chica, Pares, Juego
Mus allows card exchange before play
Betting on each category in order
First to 40 points wins the game

strategy.basic: Learn the signals to communicate with your partner. Understand the four categories and which ones your hand is strong in. Bluff occasionally to make opponents fold.
strategy.intermediate: Time your betting to maximize value. Recognize when opponent betting indicates strength or bluffing. Use Mus wisely to improve your hand.
strategy.advanced: Master the complex signal system. Read opponents' signals (if you can detect them). Calculate odds for Juego category. Expert bluffing and folding strategy.
tips: The signal system is crucial - learn it thoroughly
Do not always bet with the best hand - sometimes trap opponents
Mus can dramatically improve your hand but gives information to opponents
Ordago is risky but can end the game quickly

difficulty.easy: Random betting; no signaling; poor bluffing.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable betting; basic signaling; some bluffing.
difficulty.hard: Expert betting; full signal vocabulary; sophisticated bluffing; opponent reading.

phases.label: Betting round
phases.notes: Four rounds in order: Grande, Chica, Pares, Juego. Mano speaks first each round.

ante.reason: This game has no ante or betting.

deal.reason: Deal is performed by the dealer; not a player action.

reveal_market.reason: This game does not use a market to reveal.

buy_market.reason: This game has no market purchase.

buy_stock.reason: This game has no buying from stock.

fold.description: Concede the current category (no quiero). The betting side wins that category and takes the stones already staked; the folding side loses one stone.
fold.constraints: Only the opposing team may fold in response to a bet or raise.

check.reason: Mus uses pass (paso) instead of check; there is no bet to check.

call.description: See the current bet (quiero). Agree that the side with the best cards in this category will win the staked amount at showdown.
call.constraints: Only the opposing team may see in response to a bet or raise.

bet.description: Propose to stake stones (envido) on the current category. Minimum 2 stones; if no number stated, 2 is assumed. Mano may pass or bet first each round.
bet.constraints: Mano begins each betting round; any player may bet when it is their turn to speak.

raise.description: Raise the stake (reenvido). Propose to increase by at least 2 stones; opponents must then fold, see, or raise further.
raise.constraints: Only the opposing team may raise in response to a bet or raise.

declare.reason: This game has no declare phase.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands are not revealed in this phase.

award_pot.reason: This game has no pot to award.

play_card.reason: Mus is a vying game; cards are not played to a trick. Hands are compared at showdown after four betting rounds.

draw.reason: Draw occurs only in the Mus phase when all four agree; there is no per-turn draw-from-stock action.

discard.reason: This game has no discard pile.

pass.description: Pass (paso). Decline to bet in this round; turn passes to next player anticlockwise. If all four pass, no betting in that category and mano begins the next category.
pass.constraints: Legal when it is your turn to speak in a betting round.

bid.reason: This game has no bid action.

meld.reason: This game has no meld action.

go_out.reason: This game has no go-out action.

drawSources.notes: In Mus phase only; discard then draw equal number.

edgeCases.text: Ties in hand comparison: mano wins; if still tied, earlier player after mano in anticlockwise order wins.
Órdago: if called, game ends immediately; the 40-point target is irrelevant for that game.

customActions.description: Stake the whole game on the current category (órdago). Opponents must fold or see; if they see, immediate showdown decides the game.
customActions.constraints: Legal during any of the four betting rounds instead of a normal bet or raise.

engine.handRankingSystem: Grande (high): compare four cards descending; highest first card wins, then second, third, fourth. Chica (low): same order ascending. Pares: par simple (one pair) < medias (three of a kind) < duples (two pairs); higher rank wins within type. Juego: sum card points (R/3/C/S=10, 7-4 face, A/2=1); 31 best, then 32, 40, 37, 36, 35, 34, 33; under 31 competes as Punto (highest total under 31 wins).
engine.rankingSystem: Card order for Grande/Chica: Rey or 3 (highest), Caballo, Sota, 7, 6, 5, 4, Ace or 2 (lowest). Suits irrelevant.
engine.deckDescription: A 40-card Spanish deck with four suits and ranks 1 through 7 plus face cards (e.g. Sota, Caballo, Rey), used in many Spanish and Latin American games.
engine.suitDescription: Suits and ranks are as defined in the deck description above; no separate suit or rank set is used for this game.
